questions.question_text: Find the half range sine series of $f(x)=x$ in $0<x<l$.
questions.answer: $b_n=(2/l)\int_0^l x\sin(n\pi x/l)dx=2l(-1)^{n+1}/(n\pi)$. Thus $x=(2l/\pi)\sum_{n\ge1}(-1)^{n+1}\sin(n\pi x/l)/n$.

questions.question_text: Find the complete integral of $p(1+q)=qz$.
questions.answer: The two-parameter family $z=a+b e^{x+y/a}$ satisfies $p=b e^{x+y/a}$ and $q=p/a$, so $p(1+q)=qz$.

questions.question_text: What are the three possible solutions of one dimensional heat equation and which is the proper solution?
questions.answer: Separating $u=X(x)T(t)$ yields trigonometric, linear, or exponential spatial factors according as the separation constant is negative, zero, or positive. For a finite rod with both ends held at zero, the nontrivial admissible modes are $\sin(n\pi x/l)e^{-\alpha^2n^2\pi^2t/l^2}$; other boundary conditions can select different modes.

questions.question_text: Prove that $F\{f(x-a)\}=e^{ias}F(s)$.
questions.answer: With the positive-exponent convention $F(s)=\int f(x)e^{isx}dx$, substitute $u=x-a$ to obtain $e^{ias}F(s)$.

questions.question_text: Write the various possible solutions of $r^2u_{rr}+ru_r+u_{\theta\theta}=0$ and the suitable solution for it.
questions.answer: Separation yields the zero mode $A+B\log r+C\theta+D\theta\log r$ and, for integer $n\ge1$, $(A_nr^n+B_nr^{-n})(C_n\cos n\theta+D_n\sin n\theta)$. Periodicity removes terms linear in $\theta$; regularity at the origin removes $\log r$ and $r^{-n}$. The boundary geometry selects the remaining modes.

questions.question_text: Find the Fourier transform of $f(x)=1$ for $|x|\le1$ and $f(x)=0$ for $|x|>1$.
questions.answer: For the symmetric convention, $F(s)=\frac1{\sqrt{2\pi}}\int_{-1}^1e^{isx}dx=\sqrt{2/\pi}\,\sin s/s$, with limiting value $\sqrt{2/\pi}$ at zero.

questions.question_text: If $f(x)=x^2$, in $-\pi<x<\pi$, then find the root mean square value of the function $f(x)$.
questions.answer: $\sqrt{\frac1{2\pi}\int_{-\pi}^{\pi}x^4dx}=\pi^2/\sqrt5$.

questions.question_text: (i) Find the singular integral of $z=px+qy+p^2-q^2$. (ii) Solve $(D^2+DD\prime-6D\prime^2)z=x^2y$.
questions.answer: (i) The complete integral is $z=ax+by+a^2-b^2$. Its envelope satisfies $a=-x/2,b=y/2$, giving $z=(y^2-x^2)/4$. (ii) Factoring gives $(D-2D\prime)(D+3D\prime)$. One particular integral is $x^4y/12-x^5/60$; hence $z=\phi(y+2x)+\psi(y-3x)+x^4y/12-x^5/60$.

questions.question_text: (i) Solve $x(y^2-z^2)p+y(z^2-x^2)q=z(x^2-y^2)$. (ii) Form the partial differential equation by eliminating the arbitrary function $f$ from $z=x+y+f(xy+z)=0$.
questions.answer: (i) The characteristic equations preserve $xyz$ and $x^2+y^2+z^2$, so $\Phi(xyz,x^2+y^2+z^2)=0$. (ii) Interpreting the printed expression as $z=x+y+f(xy+z)$, differentiation yields $(p-1)/(y+p)=(q-1)/(x+q)$, or $(p-1)(x+q)=(q-1)(y+p)$. The trailing $=0$ in the scan makes the statement ambiguous.

questions.question_text: Find the Fourier series of period $2\pi$ for $f(x)=x^2-x$ in $(-\pi,\pi)$. Hence deduce the sum of the series (i) $1-1/2^2+1/3^2-\cdots$ (ii) $1+1/2^4+1/3^4+\cdots$.
questions.answer: $x^2-x=\pi^2/3+\sum_{n\ge1}[4(-1)^n\cos nx/n^2+2(-1)^n\sin nx/n]$. At $x=0$ the cosine part gives $\sum(-1)^{n+1}/n^2=\pi^2/12$. Parseval for the even function $x^2$, together with $\sum 1/n^2=\pi^2/6$, gives $\sum1/n^4=\pi^4/90$.

questions.question_text: Find the first three harmonics of the Fourier series from the following table: $x=0,\pi/3,2\pi/3,\pi,4\pi/3,5\pi/3,2\pi$; $f(x)=1.98,1.3,1.05,1.3,-0.88,-0.25,1.98$.
questions.answer: Using the six distinct observations, the trigonometric interpolant is $3/4+(28/75)\cos x+(29\sqrt3/50)\sin x+(89/100)\cos2x-(19\sqrt3/300)\sin2x-(1/30)\cos3x$. The third harmonic is the Nyquist term and has half the ordinary coefficient normalization.

questions.question_text: A tightly stretched string with fixed end points $x=0$ and $x=l$ is initially at rest in its equilibrium position. If it is set to vibrate by giving each point a velocity $v_0\sin^3(\pi x/l)$, find the displacement of any point of the string at any subsequent time.
questions.answer: Using $\sin^3\theta=(3\sin\theta-\sin3\theta)/4$ and wave speed $c$, $y=\frac{v_0l}{4\pi c}[3\sin(\pi x/l)\sin(\pi ct/l)-\frac13\sin(3\pi x/l)\sin(3\pi ct/l)]$.

questions.question_text: A rod of length $l$ has its ends A and B kept at 0°C and 100°C until steady state condition prevail. If the temperature at B is reduced suddenly to 0°C and kept so while that of A is maintained, find the temperature $u(x,t)$ at a distance $x$ from A at time $t$.
questions.answer: The initial profile is $100x/l$ and both ends subsequently vanish. Its sine coefficients are $200(-1)^{n+1}/(n\pi)$. Thus $u(x,t)=\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{200(-1)^{n+1}}{n\pi}\sin(n\pi x/l)e^{-\alpha^2n^2\pi^2t/l^2}$.
questions.chapter: Unit 3: Applications of Partial Differential Equations

questions.question_text: A semi circular plate of radius $a$ cm has insulated faces and heat flows in plane curves. The bounding diameter is kept at 0°C and the semi circumference is maintained at temperature $u(a,\theta)=50(\pi\theta-\theta^2)$ in $0\le\theta\le\pi$. Find the steady state temperature distribution.
questions.answer: Fourier sine coefficients of the boundary value are $b_n=200[1-(-1)^n]/(\pi n^3)$. The regular harmonic solution is $u(r,\theta)=\sum_{n\ge1}b_n(r/a)^n\sin n\theta$.
questions.chapter: Unit 3: Applications of Partial Differential Equations

questions.question_text: A rectangular plate with insulated surfaces is 8 cm wide and so long compared to its width that it may be considered as an infinite plate. If the temperature along short-edge $y=0$ is $u(x,0)=100\sin(\pi x/8)$, $0<x<8$, while two long edges $x=0$, $x=8$ as well as the other short edge are kept at 0°C, find the steady state temperature at any point of the plate.
questions.answer: The decaying separated harmonic solution is $u(x,y)=100e^{-\pi y/8}\sin(\pi x/8)$.

questions.question_text: Find the Fourier transform of $f(x)=a^2-x^2$ if $|x|<a$, and $f(x)=0$ if $|x|>a$. Hence prove that $\int_0^\infty(\sin x-x\cos x)/x^3\,dx=\pi/4$.
questions.answer: Under the unnormalized convention $F(s)=\int f(x)e^{-isx}dx=4[\sin(as)-as\cos(as)]/s^3$. Inversion at $x=0$ gives $a^2=(4/\pi)\int_0^\infty[\sin(as)-as\cos(as)]/s^3\,ds$; changing variable $x=as$ proves the result.

questions.question_text: (i) Evaluate $\int_0^\infty dx/[(x^2+a^2)(x^2+b^2)]$ using transform techniques. (ii) Show that $F_s(xf(x))=-\frac{d}{ds}F_c(s)$ and $F_c(xf(x))=\frac{d}{ds}F_s(s)$.
questions.answer: (i) For $a,b>0$, Parseval applied to $F_c(e^{-ax})=\sqrt{2/\pi}\,a/(a^2+s^2)$ yields $\pi/[2ab(a+b)]$. (ii) Differentiate the cosine and sine transform integrals under the integral sign to obtain the two identities.
